_about: Acronym glossary for learning sites. build.py wraps every occurrence in <abbr title>. Value = "Expansion: one-line description." A site can override or add terms in its own _glossary.json. _ignore lists capitalised words that are not acronyms (tags, keywords, names).

terms.AA: WCAG level AA: the middle conformance level, the one most laws and contracts require.
terms.ACL: Access Control List: rules that allow or deny traffic or access.
terms.ACLs: Access Control Lists: rules that allow or deny traffic or access.
terms.ACM: AWS Certificate Manager: issues and renews TLS certificates.
terms.ACR: Azure Container Registry: Azure’s private registry for container images.
terms.ADKAR: Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement: Prosci’s model for individual change.
terms.ADLS: Azure Data Lake Storage: Blob Storage with folders and permissions built for analytics.
terms.ADM: Architecture Development Method: TOGAF’s step-by-step cycle for developing an architecture.
terms.ADR: Architecture Decision Record: a short document that records one decision, its context and consequences.
terms.ADRs: Architecture Decision Records: short documents that each record one decision, its context and consequences.
terms.AFT: Account Factory for Terraform: Control Tower account vending through a Terraform pipeline.
terms.AI: Artificial Intelligence: software that does tasks that normally need human judgement.
terms.AKS: Azure Kubernetes Service: Microsoft’s managed Kubernetes. Azure runs the control plane; you run the nodes.
terms.ALB: Application Load Balancer: a layer 7 (HTTP) load balancer.
terms.AMI: Amazon Machine Image: the template an EC2 instance boots from.
terms.AMIs: Amazon Machine Images: templates EC2 instances boot from.
terms.ANI: Automatic Number Identification: the caller’s phone number, passed on by the phone network.
terms.ANSI: American National Standards Institute: US standards body. ANSI X12 is the US standard for EDI messages.
terms.API: Application Programming Interface: a defined contract that one program uses to call another.
terms.APIM: Azure API Management: Microsoft’s API gateway service.
terms.APIs: Application Programming Interfaces: defined contracts that one program uses to call another.
terms.ARC: Amazon Application Recovery Controller: tools to plan and run failover across AZs and Regions.
terms.ARIA: Accessible Rich Internet Applications: HTML attributes that describe UI roles and states to screen readers.
terms.ARM: Azure Resource Manager: Azure’s deployment layer. ARM templates are JSON infrastructure-as-code.
terms.ASC: Accredited Standards Committee: the body (ASC X12) that maintains the X12 EDI standards.
terms.ASQ: American Society for Quality: a professional body for quality management.
terms.ATAM: Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method: the SEI method to evaluate an architecture against quality goals.
terms.ATLAS: Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems: MITRE’s knowledge base of attacks on AI.
terms.AWS: Amazon Web Services: Amazon’s public cloud platform.
terms.AZ: Availability Zone: one or more separate data centres in a Region, with independent power and network.
terms.AZs: Availability Zones: separate data centres in a Region, with independent power and network.
terms.B2B: Business-to-Business: a company that sells to other companies.
terms.B2C: Business-to-Consumer. Here: Azure AD B2C, Microsoft’s older customer sign-in service.
terms.BAN: Billing Account Number: the key that identifies a customer account.
terms.BATNA: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement: what you do if the deal fails.
terms.BDD: Behaviour-Driven Development: requirements written as Given / When / Then examples that also run as tests.
terms.BFF: Backend for Frontend: a server layer built for one UI. It shapes the APIs for that UI and keeps tokens off the browser.
terms.BP: Blueprint: a numbered item in the exam blueprint.
terms.BYOK: Bring Your Own Key: a customer-supplied encryption key.
terms.C2PA: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity: the standard behind Content Credentials.
terms.C4: C4 model: Context, Containers, Components and Code diagrams, by Simon Brown.
terms.CASB: Cloud Access Security Broker: a control point that sees and governs the use of cloud apps.
terms.CC: Creative Commons: a family of open content licences.
terms.CD: Continuous Delivery: every change that passes the pipeline can go to production.
terms.CDC: Change Data Capture: streaming each database change as an event.
terms.CDK: AWS Cloud Development Kit: defines infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Java and other languages.
terms.CDN: Content Delivery Network: edge servers that cache content close to users.
terms.CDP: Customer Data Platform: a system that joins customer data from many sources.
terms.CEO: Chief Executive Officer: the top executive of a company.
terms.CI: Continuous Integration: every change is merged often and built and tested automatically.
terms.CIDR: Classless Inter-Domain Routing: an IP address range, such as 10.0.0.0/16.
terms.CIDRs: Classless Inter-Domain Routing ranges: IP address ranges, such as 10.0.0.0/16.
terms.CIO: Chief Information Officer: the executive who runs IT.
terms.CLS: Cumulative Layout Shift: Core Web Vital for unexpected page movement. Good is below 0.1.
terms.CMDB: Configuration Management Database: a record of IT assets and how they relate.
terms.CMU: Carnegie Mellon University: a US research university, home of the SEI.
terms.CNCF: Cloud Native Computing Foundation: the home of Kubernetes and related open-source projects.
terms.CNI: Container Network Interface: the plugin that gives Kubernetes pods their network. On EKS, pods get VPC IPs.
terms.CO2: Carbon dioxide. Here: emissions calculated per shipment for sustainability reporting.
terms.CoE: Centre of Excellence: a small central team that sets standards and helps others adopt a capability.
terms.CoEs: Centres of Excellence: small central teams that set standards and help others adopt a capability.
terms.CPQ: Configure, Price, Quote: software that builds valid product configurations, prices them and produces quotes.
terms.CPU: Central Processing Unit: the processor that runs program instructions.
terms.CQL: Cassandra Query Language: Cassandra’s SQL-like query language.
terms.CQRS: Command Query Responsibility Segregation: separate models for writing data and for reading it.
terms.CRA: Create React App: the old React starter tool, deprecated in February 2025.
terms.CRM: Customer Relationship Management: the system for accounts, opportunities, quotes and service cases.
terms.CSAM: Child Sexual Abuse Material: illegal content that AI policies must block.
terms.CSI: Container Storage Interface: the Kubernetes storage plug-in standard. The Secrets Store CSI driver mounts Key Vault secrets into pods.
terms.CSPM: Cloud Security Posture Management: checks cloud configuration against security standards.
terms.CSR: Client-Side Rendering: the browser builds the page with JavaScript.
terms.CXO: Chief-level executive: a CEO, CFO, CIO or similar.
terms.CXOs: Chief-level executives: CEOs, CFOs, CIOs and similar.
terms.DAM: Digital Asset Management: a system that stores and governs images, video and brand assets.
terms.DAST: Dynamic Application Security Testing: attacking a running application from outside to find vulnerabilities.
terms.DB: Database: an organised store of data.
terms.DBA: Database Administrator: the person who runs, secures and tunes databases.
terms.DC: Datacenter: in Cassandra, a logical group of nodes, usually one per region.
terms.DCs: Datacenters: in Cassandra, logical groups of nodes, usually one per region.
terms.DDD: Domain-Driven Design: modelling software around business domains, with bounded contexts as boundaries.
terms.DDoS: Distributed Denial of Service: an attack that floods a service with traffic from many sources.
terms.DLP: Data Loss Prevention: controls that detect and block sensitive data leaving the organisation.
terms.DLQ: Dead-Letter Queue: a holding queue for messages that cannot be processed.
terms.DLQs: Dead-Letter Queues: where messages go after they fail processing too many times.
terms.DLT: Dead-Letter Topic: the Kafka form of a dead-letter queue (Spring Kafka’s term).
terms.DMF: Data Management Framework: the Finance and Operations import and export engine for data entities.
terms.DMS: Database Migration Service: migrates databases and streams changes (CDC).
terms.DNS: Domain Name System: turns names into IP addresses.
terms.DORA: DevOps Research and Assessment: the research programme behind the four software delivery metrics.
terms.DPA: Data Processing Agreement: the contract that governs how a vendor processes personal data.
terms.DPIA: Data Protection Impact Assessment: a GDPR assessment of high-risk processing of personal data.
terms.DPIAs: Data Protection Impact Assessments: GDPR assessments of high-risk processing of personal data.
terms.DR: Disaster Recovery: restoring service after losing a whole site or Region.
terms.DRS: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery: continuous block-level replication of servers to AWS.
terms.DSE: DataStax Enterprise: DataStax’s commercial Cassandra distribution.
terms.DSQL: Distributed SQL: Aurora DSQL is a serverless, multi-Region distributed SQL database.
terms.DSS: Data Security Standard: PCI DSS, the card-payment security standard.
terms.DX: Developer Experience: how easy and productive it is to build software. Also a productivity research company.
terms.E2E: End-to-End: covering a whole user journey across every component.
terms.EA: Enterprise Architecture: aligning business strategy and technology across the organisation.
terms.EBS: Elastic Block Store: block volumes attached to EC2 instances.
terms.EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud: virtual servers on AWS.
terms.ECR: Elastic Container Registry: AWS’s container image registry.
terms.ECS: Elastic Container Service: AWS’s own container orchestrator.
terms.EDA: Event-Driven Architecture: services communicate by publishing events and reacting to them.
terms.EDI: Electronic Data Interchange: standard message formats that companies exchange (orders, status updates, invoices).
terms.EDIFACT: Electronic Data Interchange for Administration, Commerce and Transport: the UN’s international EDI standard.
terms.EDPB: European Data Protection Board: the EU body that issues GDPR guidance.
terms.EFS: Elastic File System: a managed NFS file system.
terms.EKS: Elastic Kubernetes Service: AWS’s managed Kubernetes.
terms.EOS: Exactly-Once Semantics: Kafka’s idempotent, transactional mode, so each record affects the output once.
terms.ERP: Enterprise Resource Planning: the system for finance, supply chain, orders and invoicing.
terms.ETA: Estimated Time of Arrival: when something is expected to arrive or finish.
terms.ETL: Extract, Transform, Load: moving data between systems while reshaping it.
terms.EU: European Union: the political and economic union of 27 European states.
terms.EVS: Amazon Elastic VMware Service: runs VMware Cloud Foundation on EC2 bare-metal instances.
terms.F&O: Finance and Operations: the shared platform under Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management.
terms.FAQ: Frequently Asked Questions: a page of common questions and answers.
terms.FID: First Input Delay: the old Core Web Vital for responsiveness, replaced by INP in March 2024.
terms.FIFO: First In, First Out: messages are delivered in the order they were sent.
terms.FinOps: Cloud financial operations: engineering, finance and business sharing ownership of cloud spend.
terms.FOCUS: FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification: an open format for cloud billing data.
terms.FSx: Amazon FSx: managed file systems such as Windows File Server, NetApp ONTAP and Lustre.
terms.FTE: Full-Time Equivalent: one person working full time.
terms.GA: General Availability: the product is fully released and supported.

terms.GCP: Google Cloud Platform: Google’s public cloud.
terms.GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation: the EU law on personal data.
terms.GenAI: Generative AI: models that produce text, images or code.
terms.GPT: Generative Pre-trained Transformer: the model design behind many large language models.
terms.GPU: Graphics Processing Unit: used for AI training and inference.
terms.GRC: Governance, Risk and Compliance: how an organisation sets rules, manages risk and proves it follows the law.
terms.HA: High Availability: a design that keeps a service running when parts fail.
terms.HELM: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models: Stanford’s benchmark suite for language models.
terms.HIPAA: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act: the US law that protects health information.
terms.HPA: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler: Kubernetes controller that adds or removes pods based on metrics.
terms.HPC: High-Performance Computing: large clusters that run compute-heavy jobs.
terms.HR: Human Resources: the function that manages people and employment.
terms.HTML: HyperText Markup Language: the structure language of web pages.
terms.HTTP: Hypertext Transfer Protocol: the request and response protocol of the web.
terms.HTTPS: HTTP over TLS: encrypted web traffic.
terms.IA: Infrequent Access: a cheaper S3 storage class for data that is read rarely.
terms.IaC: Infrastructure as Code: defining infrastructure in version-controlled files.
terms.IAM: Identity and Access Management: AWS’s service for users, roles and permission policies.
terms.IBM: International Business Machines: the US technology company.
terms.ICO: Information Commissioner’s Office: the UK data protection regulator.
terms.ID: Identifier: a value that names one record or thing.
terms.IDE: Integrated Development Environment: a code editor with build, run and debug tools.

terms.IDs: Identifiers: values that name one record or thing each.
terms.IEC: International Electrotechnical Commission: a standards body that publishes jointly with ISO.
terms.IFTSTA: An EDIFACT message type: International Forwarding and Transport Status report.
terms.INP: Interaction to Next Paint: Core Web Vital for responsiveness. Good is below 200 ms.
terms.IOPS: Input/Output Operations Per Second: a storage performance measure.
terms.IP: Internet Protocol: the addressing scheme for networked machines; here, an IP address.
terms.IPAM: IP Address Management: VPC IPAM plans and tracks IP ranges across accounts.
terms.IPs: Internet Protocol addresses: the numeric addresses of networked machines.

terms.ISE: Integration Service Environment: a retired isolated hosting option for Azure Logic Apps.
terms.ISO: International Organization for Standardization: the body that publishes international standards.
terms.ISR: In-Sync Replicas: Kafka replicas that are fully caught up with the partition leader.
terms.IT: Information Technology: the systems and the team that run them.
terms.ITSM: IT Service Management: tools and processes for incidents, changes and requests.
terms.IVR: Interactive Voice Response: the phone menu system that callers use before they reach an agent.
terms.JD: Job Description: the employer’s description of a role and its requirements.

terms.JDs: Job Descriptions: employers’ descriptions of roles and their requirements.

terms.JS: JavaScript: the programming language of web browsers.
terms.JSON: JavaScript Object Notation: a lightweight text format for data.
terms.JTC: Joint Technical Committee: here, CEN-CENELEC JTC 21, which writes the standards for the EU AI Act.
terms.JVM: Java Virtual Machine: the runtime that executes Java bytecode.
terms.JWT: JSON Web Token: a signed token that carries identity claims.
terms.JWTs: JSON Web Token: a signed token that carries identity claims.

terms.KEDA: Kubernetes Event-Driven Autoscaling: scales workloads on event sources such as Kafka consumer lag.
terms.KIP: Kafka Improvement Proposal: the design process for changes to Apache Kafka.
terms.KMS: Key Management Service: creates and controls encryption keys.
terms.KPI: Key Performance Indicator: a measure that shows progress toward a goal.
terms.KPIs: Key Performance Indicators: measures that show progress toward goals.
terms.KRaft: Kafka Raft: Kafka’s built-in consensus for cluster metadata. It replaced ZooKeeper.
terms.L&D: Learning and Development: the function that runs staff training.
terms.L4: Layer 4 (transport layer): load balancing on TCP/UDP connections, without reading HTTP.
terms.L7: Layer 7 (application layer): load balancing that reads HTTP (paths, headers, cookies).
terms.LB: Load Balancer: spreads traffic across several servers.
terms.LCP: Largest Contentful Paint: Core Web Vital for loading speed. Good is below 2.5 s.
terms.LCS: Lifecycle Services: the older Microsoft portal for managing Finance and Operations projects and environments.
terms.LGTM: Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir: Grafana’s open-source stack for logs, dashboards, traces and metrics.
terms.LLM: Large Language Model: an AI model trained on large text corpora to understand and generate language.
terms.LLMs: Large Language Models: AI models trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language.
terms.LOCODE: Location Code: UN/LOCODE, five-character codes for ports and trade locations (e.g. USNYC).
terms.LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation: a cheap fine-tuning method that trains small added weight matrices.
terms.LTS: Long-Term Support: a release with a longer support window.
terms.LZA: Landing Zone Accelerator: an AWS solution that deploys a compliance-aligned multi-account baseline from config files.
terms.M&A: Mergers and Acquisitions: companies buying or combining with other companies.
terms.MAP: Migration Acceleration Program: AWS’s funded methodology for large migrations, delivered with partners.
terms.MCP: Model Context Protocol: an open standard for connecting AI agents to tools and data.
terms.MCPs: Model Context Protocol servers: services that expose tools and data to AI applications.
terms.MDN: MDN Web Docs (formerly Mozilla Developer Network): Mozilla’s web developer reference.
terms.METR: Model Evaluation and Threat Research: a non-profit that studies AI capabilities and their effects.
terms.MFA: Multi-Factor Authentication: a sign-in that needs two or more proofs of identity.
terms.MGN: AWS Application Migration Service: block-level replication for lift-and-shift (rehost) migrations.
terms.MI: Managed Instance: here, Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra.
terms.MIT: Massachusetts Institute of Technology: a US research university.
terms.MITRE: MITRE Corporation: a US non-profit that runs security frameworks such as ATT&CK and ATLAS.
terms.ML: Machine Learning: models that learn patterns from data.
terms.MQ: Message Queue: a service that stores messages until a consumer reads them.

terms.MSK: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka: AWS’s managed Kafka service.
terms.NAT: Network Address Translation: lets private resources start outbound internet connections.
terms.NCSC: National Cyber Security Centre: the UK’s cyber security authority.
terms.NFR: Non-Functional Requirement: a quality target such as latency, availability, security or cost.
terms.NFRs: Non-Functional Requirement: a quality target such as latency, availability, security or cost.
terms.NIST: National Institute of Standards and Technology: the US standards body.
terms.NLB: Network Load Balancer: AWS’s layer-4 load balancer.
terms.NoSQL: “Not only SQL”: databases that do not use the relational table model.
terms.NSGs: Network Security Group: Azure firewall rules on a subnet or network interface.
terms.OAuth: Open Authorization: the standard for delegated access with tokens.
terms.OAuth2: OAuth 2.0: the current version of the Open Authorization standard.
terms.OCSF: Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework: an open standard schema for security data.
terms.OData: Open Data Protocol: a REST-based standard for querying and updating data over HTTP.
terms.ODS: Operational Data Store: a current-state copy of operational data, built for fast reads.
terms.OECD: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development: an intergovernmental body that publishes AI policy principles.
terms.OIDC: OpenID Connect: an identity layer on OAuth 2.0, used to federate CI pipelines into AWS roles.
terms.OMS: Order Management System: captures, splits, sources and tracks orders through fulfilment.
terms.OPA: Open Policy Agent: a general policy engine.
terms.OS: Operating System: the base software that runs a computer.
terms.OSS: Open Source Software: here, the open-source edition of Redis.
terms.OTel: OpenTelemetry: the vendor-neutral standard for metrics, logs and traces.
terms.OU: Organizational Unit: a group of accounts in AWS Organizations. Policies attach to it.
terms.OUs: Organizational Units: groups of accounts in AWS Organizations. Policies attach to them.
terms.OWASP: Open Worldwide Application Security Project: a nonprofit that publishes security guidance such as the Top 10.
terms.P&L: Profit and Loss: a statement or budget of income and costs.

terms.PaaS: Platform as a Service: the cloud runs the platform; you deploy only your code or data.
terms.PCI: Payment Card Industry: PCI DSS is the security standard for handling card data.
terms.PDBs: PodDisruptionBudget: limits how many pods may be down at once during planned disruption.
terms.PDF: Portable Document Format: a fixed-layout document file. Here, the bill image.
terms.PEFT: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: methods that adapt a model by training only a small set of parameters.
terms.PII: Personally Identifiable Information: data that can identify a person.

terms.Q&A: Questions and Answers: a session or document of questions with answers.
terms.QA: Quality Assurance: the practice of testing that work meets its standard.
terms.QLDB: Quantum Ledger Database: an AWS ledger database, ended 31 Jul 2025.
terms.RACI: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed: a matrix of who does what.
terms.RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: the model answers from documents retrieved at query time.
terms.RAID: Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies: a project control log.
terms.RAM: Resource Access Manager: shares resources such as Transit Gateways across accounts.

terms.RDS: Relational Database Service: managed relational databases.

terms.REST: Representational State Transfer: an HTTP API style built around resources.
terms.RF: Replication Factor: how many copies of each piece of data the cluster keeps.
terms.RFC: Request for Comments: the IETF’s standards documents.
terms.RFI: Request for Information: a short questionnaire sent to vendors before a formal tender.
terms.ROI: Return on Investment: the gain from an investment compared with its cost.
terms.RPO: Recovery Point Objective: the most data loss that is acceptable, measured in time.
terms.RTO: Recovery Time Objective: the longest acceptable time to restore service.
terms.RU: Request Unit: Cosmos DB’s unit of cost for each operation.

terms.RUs: Request Unit: Cosmos DB’s unit of cost for each operation.
terms.SaaS: Software as a Service: software you rent and use over the internet.
terms.SAI: Storage-Attached Indexing: Cassandra 5.0’s improved secondary indexes.
terms.SAM: Serverless Application Model: short-form CloudFormation for serverless apps.
terms.SAP: SAP SE: the German enterprise software company; its ERP is S/4HANA.
terms.SASL: Simple Authentication and Security Layer: the framework Kafka uses for client authentication.
terms.SAST: Static Application Security Testing: scanning source code for vulnerabilities.
terms.SBMP: Service Bus Messaging Protocol: an older Azure Service Bus protocol, retiring.
terms.SBOM: Software Bill of Materials: the list of every component in a build.

terms.SCPs: Service Control Policies: Organizations policies that cap what IAM principals in member accounts can do. They never grant.
terms.SDK: Software Development Kit: libraries and tools for building against a platform.
terms.SDKs: Software Development Kits: libraries and tools for building against a platform.
terms.SDLC: Software Development Life Cycle: plan, build, test, release, operate.
terms.SEI: Software Engineering Institute: the Carnegie Mellon research centre that created ATAM.
terms.SEO: Search Engine Optimisation: making pages rank well in search results.
terms.SKU: Stock Keeping Unit: a unique code for one product or licence item.
terms.SLA: Service Level Agreement: a committed service level, often with penalties.
terms.SLAs: Service Level Agreement: a contractual commitment to a service level, with penalties if missed.

terms.SLIs: Service Level Indicator: a measured ratio of good events to all events.
terms.SLO: Service Level Objective: the target for an SLI, e.g. 99.9% over 30 days.
terms.SLOs: Service Level Objectives: targets for reliability, such as 99.9% of requests under 300 ms.
terms.SMS: Short Message Service: mobile text messages.

terms.SNS: Simple Notification Service: managed pub/sub topics.

terms.SOX: Sarbanes-Oxley Act: the US law on controls over financial reporting.

terms.SPACE: Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Communication, Efficiency: a framework for developer productivity.
terms.SQL: Structured Query Language: the standard language for relational databases.
terms.SQS: Simple Queue Service: managed message queues.
terms.SRE: Site Reliability Engineering: running operations with software engineering, driven by SLOs and error budgets.
terms.SSE: Security Service Edge: cloud-delivered security for web, cloud apps and private access.
terms.SSG: Static Site Generation: pages built once at build time.

terms.TUs: Throughput Unit: Event Hubs capacity unit on the Standard tier.
terms.TV: Television: here, a subscription TV provider (satellite and cable).

terms.XML: Extensible Markup Language: a tagged text format for data.
terms.XSS: Cross-Site Scripting: an attack that injects script into pages other users see.
terms.YAML: YAML Ain’t Markup Language: a human-readable configuration format.
terms.ZAP: Zed Attack Proxy: OWASP’s open-source tool for dynamic security testing.
terms.S3: Simple Storage Service: Amazon’s object storage service.
terms.D365: Dynamics 365: Microsoft’s suite of CRM and ERP business applications.
terms.CLI: Command-Line Interface: a tool you drive by typing commands.
